problems.problem: The prompt revision did not land: the diagonal fold still renders as a saturated teal wedge, not a whisper-darker paper crease. In the current poster a hard-edged band of roughly #2e7ea6, ~18-30px wide, runs from behind the bottle's right flank (x≈590, y≈1130) down to the bottom-right corner, plus a hairline crease entering the left edge at y≈810; the abrupt upper edge and the saturation jump against the #bfd6de field read as a printed graphic stripe. It also contradicts the declared broad soft frontal light: a matte paper sweep under diffuse frontal light cannot cast a crisp saturated edge. No softboxes, lamps, stands or cameras are present, so the fault is purely fold hardness/saturation.

Contact detail crop [132,1141,668,1391] confirms the bottle IS seated: a soft grey smudge hugs the base at canvas y≈1276-1292, so offset_y 0 is correct and must not be moved, and base y=1281 (89% of canvas) respects the margins. However the smudge spans only x≈290-500 against the 376px base footprint (bbox 212-588) and stays very low in contrast, so at poster scale the dark glass still reads slightly pasted onto the sweep. The cue needs width and presence, not repositioning.

The right-anchored stack (logo y79, title y168, subtitle y300, rule y324) still ends ~957px above the bottle base, leaving the mid-right field between the rule and the fold empty; type and product read as two islands joined only by the diagonal. text_product_overlap is false for all three blocks, so this is mass/scale, not collision: against references that deploy type as a confident graphic block (Prada's oversized serif mass), Georgia at 46px on a 1080px canvas remains modest and the diagonal grid loses its counterweight.
